# core/

Cross-cutting infrastructure catch-all: company/user/audit, currency, OCR/VLM, AI categorisation, document storage, PayFast gateway, migration wizard, Sage import/sync, job queue, email, webhooks. Not one module — services that don't belong in AR/AP/bank/gl/etc.

## Modules
- **Tenancy**: `companyService.ts` (listCompanies NOT tenant-scoped — admin only), `companyMapper.ts`, `companySettingsService.ts`, `businessUnitService.ts`, `costCentreService.ts`.
- **Users / invitations**: `userAccessService.ts`, `userInvitationService.ts`, `inviteEmailService.ts`.
- **Audit / search**: `auditTrailService.ts` (`logAudit` fire-and-forget, never throws), `globalSearchService.ts`, `nlQueryService.ts` + `nlQueryValidationService.ts` (NL→SQL with validator gate).
- **Currency / budget**: `currencyService.ts`, `multiCurrencyService.ts`, `budgetService.ts`.

- **AI invoice pipeline + categorisation**: `aiInvoicePipelineService.ts`, `aiCategorizationService.ts`, `smartCategorizationService.ts` (rules → patterns → history three-strategy), `smartCategorizationMatchingService.ts`, `smartCategorizationLearningService.ts`.
- **Duplicates / anomalies**: `duplicateDetectionService.ts`, `duplicateMergeService.ts`, `anomalyDetectionService.ts`.
- **Evidence / recurring**: `evidenceGraphService.ts` (TB→JE→document drill, PRD-05 Phase 2), `recurringTransactionService.ts` + `recurringTransactionInvoices.ts` (its AR/AP branches) + `recurringTemplateLock.ts` (the template row lock).

- **Payment gateway (PayFast)**: `paymentGatewayCore.ts`, `paymentGatewayService.ts` (facade: `handleITN`, `enableOnlinePayment`), `paymentGatewayItnService.ts`, `paymentGatewayPortalService.ts`.
- **Migration wizard**: `migrationService.ts`, `migrationCoaService.ts` (+ `migrationCoaSubtype.ts`, the row→subtype rule; `migrationCoaVatLock.ts`, the before/after attribute snapshots its VAT-lock check reads), `migrationContactService.ts`, `migrationImportService.ts`, `migrationParserService.ts`, `migrationTemplateService.ts`, `migrationExecuteService.ts`, `migrationOpeningBalanceService.ts` (opening trial balance → one journal; all-or-nothing), `migrationRollbackService.ts` (per-account DELETE in its own savepoint: a 23503 retains that account and clears its `imported_from`, never aborts the run), `migrationValidationService.ts`.

## Caller contract
Invoked by `withCompany`-wrapped API routes in `pages/api/accounting/**`. Most functions take `companyId` first; exceptions: `companyService.listCompanies` (admin, returns all), `jobQueueService` (job rows carry their own `company_id`), `userInvitationService` (invitations are orgless at create time).

## Main function signatures
- `createCompany(input) / updateCompany(id, input)`; `createInvitation(companyId, email, role) / acceptInvitation(token)`.
- `logAudit({ companyId, entity, action, before?, after?, userId })` — never throws.
- `requireRequestTransaction(fnName)` (`requestTransaction.ts`) — the ALS-bound client, or a THROW naming the caller. Every `FOR UPDATE` helper needs it: outside a request transaction Postgres runs the SELECT in an implicit one, releases the lock at the end of the statement and discards the surrounding `SET LOCAL lock_timeout`, so the lock reads as taken, protects nothing, and waits forever. `paymentLock`, `bankTxLock`, `creditNoteLock` and `supplierInvoiceLock` predate it and keep their own copies.
- `uploadDocument({ companyId, file, entityId?, entityType? })` — validates magic bytes, enforces entity ownership.
- `entityIdsWithDocuments(companyId, entityType, ids)` (`documentQueryService.ts`) → the subset of `ids` with at least one active document, direct or via `document_links`; one query per page; an id counts only when it is a row of `entityType`'s own table in this company (the `owned` CTE fence).
- `resolveAccountEvidence(companyId, accountId, period)` / `resolveJournalEntryEvidence(companyId, jeId)` — PRD-05 drill.
- `categorizeBankTransaction(companyId, tx) / bulkCategorize(companyId, txs)` — pre-loads rules/patterns once per bulk.
- `enqueueJob({ jobType, payload, companyId })` / `getNextJob(jobTypes?)` / `markJobComplete / markJobFailed`.
- `enableOnlinePayment(companyId, invoiceId)` → payment link URL, or null (nothing written) for an invoice that is not this company's, cancelled, soft-deleted or fully paid; `handleITN(payload)` → payment confirmation + GL post.
- `importLedgerTransactions(companyId, userId) / importSupplierInvoices(companyId, userId)` — Sage Phase 6 importers.

## Business rules
- **Cost centres and business units have ONE write path each** (#678 review, 2026-10-09): `gl/dimensions/dimensionMasterService` / `dimensionMasterEdit` for cost centres (the payroll routes too — `createCostCentre` / `updateCostCentre` / `deactivateCostCentre` / `createGlCostCentre` / `updateGlCostCentre` / `toggleCostCentre` are gone), `businessUnitService` plan/apply for BUs (`toggleBusinessUnit` is gone; create validates in `planCreateBusinessUnit`). Every one takes `dimensionMasterLock.lockDimensionMasters(companyId)` first. See `gl/dimensions/.claude.md`.
- **Lock order**: the canonical sequence for every settlement path (bank line → payment → invoices → GL) lives in `bank/.claude.md`. Read it before adding a lock here; a path that takes two of these rows out of sequence deadlocks against one that does not (40P01 → 500).

- **User identity is a STRING, never a uuid.** `users.id` is `character varying`; `company_users.user_id` is `text`. NEVER write `user_id = ${x}::UUID` or `users.id = ${x}::UUID` — Postgres has no `text = uuid` operator, so it throws at RUNTIME (500), and neither `tsc` nor eslint can see inside a SQL template string. When joining a uuid column onto `users.id`, cast the **uuid** side: `ON u.id = t.approved_by::TEXT`. `company_id` IS a uuid and keeps its cast. Guarded by `scripts/ci/audit-user-id-casts.ts` (static) + `tests/integration/user-id-join-compat.int.test.ts` (schema probe).
- **Tenant-membership guards live in `companyAccessService`** — `userBelongsToCompany` / `userBelongsToGroup`. Do not re-inline them into API routes; four routes each kept their own broken copy before this was extracted.
- `listCompanies` and other admin-only calls must NOT appear in tenant-scoped API paths — enforce via route selection.
- `logAudit` is fire-and-forget: callers don't await failure; service swallows its own errors to keep write-paths unblocked (but no empty `catch` — logs via `log`).
- **`audit_log` is append-only (R-035 N1b A, migration 880).** No role but the table's owner holds UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or TRIGGER; INSERT and SELECT stay. Never write an app path that updates, deletes or locks (`FOR UPDATE`/`FOR SHARE`) audit rows — it 500s with 42501, and `tests/unit/services/core/auditLogAppendOnlyCensus.test.ts` fails first. A later migration that re-grants an erase privilege, grants app_user/platform_admin a role, moves the owner, or rewrites audit rows is refused by the same census (a real data repair changes the census on purpose). A forged extra INSERT is still possible: append-only, not authenticated. "No role but the owner" is a statement about the catalogue, not the app's login role: the app logs in as a member of the owner and drops to app_user with `SET LOCAL ROLE`, so a connection that never does (a script, a cron pool) or SQL that can `RESET ROLE` still erases (the N1 boundary, N3); a company delete still cascades its rows. POPIA erasure of audit rows now needs the owner (a migration or an owner-equivalent connection).
- **company_users and company_invitations enforce the app's role rules in the database (R-035 N1b C, migration 883).** BEFORE row guards judge `current_user`: as `app_user` the actor (`auth.uid()`) must be an owner or admin of the company; roles come from the allow-lists (members: owner/admin/manager/viewer; invitations: also storeman/technician); only an owner grants `owner` — by role change, membership insert, or invitation, and only an owner re-points (email, token, GoTrue user) or re-opens (accepted_at, expires_at) an invitation that stays `owner` (Hein, 2026-10-09: the company-invitations route refuses an admin's owner invite too); the last owner is never demoted or removed — counted by person (a case-variant duplicate row is the same user) under a per-company advisory lock, so two owners demoting each other at once cannot both pass; nobody removes themselves; only `role` of a membership ever changes; an invitation records its sender. As `platform_admin` (admin portal): never `owner` (ALLOWED_COMPANY_ROLES), and no invitation writes. Every other role (the owners, migration_admin for invite-accept and provisioning, the definer functions, seed scripts) is not judged. A new writer of either table must say which role it writes as — `tests/unit/services/core/companyMemberWriteCensus.test.ts` fails until it is classified. Unchanged on purpose (allowed today): an admin changing their own role below owner, demoting or removing a non-last owner; the admin portal has no last-owner rule (it takes the same lock, so an app demotion racing it is judged after it). 883 refuses to apply while any live, unaccepted owner invitation exists (its sender cannot be trusted: `invited_by` was writable) — cancel them first; an owner re-issues them afterwards. Named limits: a phantom owner row (a `user_id` that is no user, written by an owner's raw SQL) still counts as an owner. Raw SQL that forges the claims GUC or can `RESET ROLE` is the N1 boundary (N3). Since 886 (PR #691 round 5, PR #693 reviews): every `app_user` write to either table is refused (40001) at any isolation level but READ COMMITTED / READ UNCOMMITTED (Postgres runs it as READ COMMITTED) — every rule reads the snapshot, which only READ COMMITTED re-takes; SERIALIZABLE too, as SSI cannot see the app's READ COMMITTED writers. The refusal comes after the rule checks, so a rule's own code (RC001–RC009) wins; the admin portal is not refused. Owner-ness has one definition, `public.company_member_role_is_owner(role)` (lower-cased, every ASCII and Unicode whitespace character removed — an explicit class, as `\s` depends on the collation — all under COLLATE "C", so the result never does), used by both guards and by the two invite-accept routes (`/api/invite/[token]`, `/api/invitations/[token]/accept`), which never overwrite an owner's role (`ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE … WHERE public.company_member_role_is_owner(company_users.role) IS NOT TRUE`) — an admin may re-invite any address at a lesser role, the owner's own included; the invitation is still accepted. 886 refuses to apply while any row of either table holds an owner-ish role other than exactly `owner` (correct by hand; it locks company_users, then company_invitations — an invite acceptance's order, so a deploy waits for one instead of deadlocking), which is what keeps the exact allow-lists, the exact count of the other owners and the portal's exact lock sound.
- `documentStorageService`: magic-byte check runs before S3 put; entity ownership verified against `companyId` before linking. Entity type `supplier_invoice` is a `supplier_invoices.id` (the bill page's id) — never `sage_supplier_invoices`, which is Sage import staging. The fence, the extraction predicate, the PO/GRN auto-link and the `procurement_documents` RLS policy must name the same parent table per type.
- `jobQueueService`: concurrent workers safe via `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; lifecycle `pending → running → completed|failed`.
- PayFast ITN: validated via HMAC signature in `paymentGatewayCore`; idempotency via PayFast transaction id.
- Evidence graph is read-only — joins GL lines back to `captured_documents` / `extracted_data`.
- Sage import uses savepoints per record so one bad row doesn't roll back the whole run; dates coerced Date→ISO (2026-04-24 fix).
- **Migration opening balances are signed against the account's normal side.** In `ParsedAccount.openingBalance` a positive figure sits on the account's own normal side and a negative one on the opposite side (a bank in overdraft, a supplier in debit, a negative contra). `migrationOpeningBalanceService.postOpeningBalances` and `migrationExecuteService.verifyBalances` (`isaflowBalance = normal_balance === 'debit' ? net_debit : -net_debit`) share that convention — change one and you must change the other. A debit-signed source export is not importable and the totals check refuses it. `postOpeningBalances` is all-or-nothing: an unresolved account, an account this source does not own (`imported_from !== source`, which is also how a rolled-back account is released back to the company), or a source that does not foot throws before anything is written. The separate wizard path (`migrationImportService.importOpeningBalances` → `openingBalancePostingService`) takes explicit debit/credit columns instead and rejects negatives outright.
- 2026-04-24: RLS guard on company creation (mig 351) unblocked via onboarding fix.
- 2026-04-24: silent swallow-catch fallbacks stripped across AR/AP APIs — errors now propagate.

## Smart-categorize sweep scope (Hein, 2026-10-21: the server is overloaded)
`smartCategorizeForAccount` (the "Apply rules" click) categorizes only `selectSweepLineIds`: status `imported`, no `suggested_gl_account_id` / `suggested_category`, no `categorization_decisions` row, dated (SAST day) OR imported in the last 30 days, newest first, max 200 **per bank account per request** (a company is bounded only by the AI rate limit, 20 requests). Lines an earlier sweep tried in the last 24 h (`categorizeSweepAttempts.ts`, in-process, forgotten on restart) sort last, so unmatchable lines cannot hold the batch and older untried lines get reached. The LLM residual pass reads only the sweep's first-attempt lines. An explicit `transactionIds` request is refused above 200 ids (400) but is not held to the recent / uncoded filters. Limits: `categorizeSweepScope.ts`.

Side effect to know before reading the metrics: a line that already carries a low-confidence suggestion is no longer re-sent to the LLM on a later click (the sweep skips suggested lines). Before 21 Oct it was. A dip in auto-coded % or accepted % after this change is the scope, not the LLM.

### Widening the sweep later
- Set `CATEGORIZE_SWEEP_RECENT_DAYS` (default 30), `CATEGORIZE_SWEEP_MAX_LINES` (default 200) and/or `CATEGORIZE_SWEEP_RETRY_HOURS` (default 24) in the service env and restart; a bad or non-positive value falls back to the default. Change the `*_DEFAULT` constants only to move the baseline for everyone.
- Widen one step at a time. Watch box load (`uptime`), smart-categorize request time (the client aborts at 15 s), LLM spend (the residual pass follows `MAX_LLM_CALLS_PER_RUN` / `DAILY_LLM_CEILING`), and the coding metrics (auto-coded %, suggestions accepted %).
- To give old low-confidence suggestions an LLM second opinion again, add a bounded second selector for recent lines with `suggested_confidence < RESIDUAL_CONFIDENCE_CEILING`; do not drop the uncoded filter.
- Index candidates: idx_bt_company_date `(company_id, transaction_date DESC, amount DESC)` (bank account and status are filtered after it), the (company_id, status, created_at) index, categorization_decisions_tx_idx. No EXPLAIN on a large tenant is recorded yet: run one before widening, and before dropping the date window altogether.

- 2026-10-03 (R-186; the r183-r187 goal file's default, not put to Hein): **the archive skips customer invoices a Paystack or Stitch payment request of the same company references, and reports how many** (`ArchiveResult.invoicesSkipped`, `ArchivePreview.customerInvoicesSkipped`, shown under the page's preview). Deleting one raised 23514 (`paystack_pr_invoice_has_invoice` / `stitch_pr_invoice_has_invoice`: both FKs are ON DELETE SET NULL) and rolled the whole run back. `archiveCustomerInvoiceScope`: `selectArchivableCustomerInvoices` picks the ids (unlocked read, so the lock order is unchanged); `countArchivableCustomerInvoices` is the preview's SQL count over the same predicate; `moveCustomerInvoicesToArchive` deletes and archives in ONE statement (`WITH moved AS (DELETE … RETURNING *) INSERT … SELECT FROM moved`) and re-applies BOTH `eligibleInvoice` and `NOT gatewayReferenced`, so an invoice reopened or re-dated since the selection, or one a payment request was opened on since, stays; if it moved fewer rows than it selected, or archived fewer than it deleted, it throws `ArchiveSetChangedError` (`ARCHIVE_SET_CHANGED`) and the run rolls back whole. A skipped invoice keeps its journals: when its `gl_journal_entry_id` (no FK) or any journal in its reversal chain (`reversal_of_id`, both directions, same company) is one the run would move (posted, before the cutoff), the run refuses with `ArchiveSkippedInvoiceJournalError` (`ARCHIVE_SKIPPED_INVOICE_JOURNAL`) before deleting anything, and `validateArchive` reports the same count (`countSkippedInvoiceJournalsInWindow`, seeded from the ids the selection skipped, so an invoice changed in between cannot escape). Today's `cancelCustomerInvoice` NULLs `gl_journal_entry_id` and keeps both journals 'posted', so a cancelled skipped invoice refers to no journal and the run moves both (pinned in `r186-archive-current-cancel`); the refusal bites on invoices that still point at a journal (paid, or legacy cancels). Receipts, their journals, the gateway fee journal and matched bank lines are NOT kept out: a receipt journal in the window still fails the run whole on 23503 `customer_payments_gl_journal_entry_id_fkey` (R-053 class). Neither refusal maps to a 4xx today; the route refuses POST (403) before calling `executeArchive`, so whoever re-enables archiving must map both codes to 409. The lock wait's `ROW_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (`RowLockTimeoutError`) is a held row, not a refusal: it must answer 503 + Retry-After, like the other D8 routes, via `respondIfLockTimeout` (`@/lib/apiDocumentLock`), which `withErrorHandler` already applies to any `*_LOCK_TIMEOUT`. Never 409 or 500. **Product consequence (for Hein):** a GL-posted paid invoice keeps its `gl_journal_entry_id`, and that journal stays 'posted' on the invoice date, before the cutoff. So under option (b) the run refuses whole for ANY company with a GL-posted invoice before the cutoff that a payment request references: such a company cannot archive until R-053/R-191 are redesigned. Its receipt journal would fail the run on 23503 anyway (R-053). A skipped invoice lets the run complete only when no journal of its chain is posted before the cutoff: cancelled by today's service (link NULLed), a legacy chain outside the window, or paid with no journal and no receipt. The full table is in R-186 fix.md. The eligibility and gateway predicates are each defined ONCE (`eligibleInvoice`, `gatewayReferenced`, nested `sql` fragments) and spliced into the selection, the preview count and the move; "the run moves this journal" is ONE fragment too (`movedJournal`, over `je`), spliced into steps 1, 2 and 6 and the refusal count. The selection and the refusal run at step 0, before anything is copied (reads only, lock order unchanged); the refusal count runs AGAIN right after the invoice move and before the GL deletes, with the skipped invoices held FOR SHARE (`lockSkippedInvoices`, bounded like the D8 locks: `ROW_LOCK_BUDGET_MS`, then `RowLockTimeoutError`). The lock protects the INVOICE ROW only: a link written since step 0 is seen, and none can be written until the run ends. A chain journal posted between step 1 and the second count IS caught (the run refuses). Any chain journal posted, or re-dated into the window, AFTER the second count, the invoice's own linked journal included, is deleted without a copy (R-192 class). A request in another company naming this company's invoice used to fail the run on 23514; since R-195 (migration 854) such a request is refused at insert. Also NOT covered: (R-194) an archived invoice's items, views, disputes and dunning sends go by CASCADE with no archive table. Pre-existing and NOT covered: (R-192) steps 1/2/3/5 copy and step 6 deletes by predicate in separate statements, so a supplier invoice, bank line or journal that changes in between is lost or left as a stale copy; (R-191) steps 1, 2 and 6 move every posted pre-cutoff journal by date, including journals of live invoices the run never selects, which then point at the archive. Requests are never archived or deleted. The RLS policy on the request tables admits every company the user belongs to, so the `company_id` predicate (not RLS) stops another company's request from shielding an invoice; such a cross-tenant reference can no longer be stored (R-195). `archive_runs` has no skipped column; the count is in the audit metadata and the log. Tests: `tests/integration/r186-archive-skips-paystack-invoices.int.test.ts` (runs as app_user), `r186-archive-move-race.int.test.ts`, `r186-archive-skipped-closure.int.test.ts`, `r186-archive-paystack-settled.int.test.ts`.

- 2026-09-24 (archiving switched off, Hein): **`POST /api/accounting/data-archiving` refuses (403) for every role, and the page no longer offers Archive Now.** `executeArchive` deletes pre-cutoff posted journals, reconciled bank lines and settled invoices into `archive_*` tables that NO report reads, so every trial balance, balance sheet and VAT201 before the cutoff would lose that history. The service is kept, because its integration tests pin the delete order. Re-enable only with a design that keeps the reports whole (e.g. closing-balance roll-forward journals before the delete). - 2026-09-24 (soft delete vs cancel): **soft-deleting a bill is held to the cancel plan.** `assertInvoiceDeletable` runs `ap/planSupplierInvoiceCancel` for any `supplier_invoice` not already `cancelled`, after its own amount_paid/allocation checks, and re-raises a `SupplierInvoiceCancelRefusal` as `SoftDeleteRefusalError` (400). A delete reverses the approval journal and takes the bill out of AP exactly as a cancel does, so without this it bypassed every refusal #486 put on the UI Cancel: bank-matched, another posted journal sourced from the bill (DRC), a draft linked journal, approved with no journal (Sage imports). Deleting a cancelled bill stays allowed. Customer invoices are unchanged.

- 2026-09-24 (VAT period lock): the COA import (`migrationCoaService.importChartOfAccounts`) runs its writes inside a savepoint and then checks the attributes it ACTUALLY wrote — every existing account's type/subtype before vs after (`migrationCoaVatLock.ts`: `accountAttributes` / `attributeChanges`) — with `gl/vatLockLineClassification.assertAccountChangesKeepVatLocks`, all changes together; if a posted line inside an active VAT lock would move (its box, or its journal into/out of the return) the savepoint rolls back and the import is refused whole, naming account and period. The row→subtype rule is shared via `migrationCoaSubtype.ts`. `migrationExecuteService.executeMigration` checks a same-source re-import's re-types before its first write.
- 2026-09-24 (R-101): **The Sage customer-invoice importer runs for the first time.** It is the AR twin of R-021 and follows the same rules: it reads only `sage_id, invoice_number, customer_name, invoice_date, total_amount`; the invoice goes to the ONE live customer of that name (case-insensitive, ends trimmed — inner spacing must match); the due date is the invoice date plus that customer's `payment_terms` days; there is no VAT and the review note is set (`deriveSageVat(null, null, total)`); it is unpaid and `approved`; the run holds `lockMigrationImport`, and each row runs in its own savepoint. The differences come from the schema. `customer_invoices` has no `sage_invoice_id`, so the Sage id is stored as `external_ref` with `external_system = 'sage'` and the Sage number as `external_document_number` (migration 530). The invoice number is unique per COMPANY, soft-deleted and cancelled rows included, so any holder of the number that is not this customer's live, in-AR invoice (not draft, pending approval or cancelled) with the same Sage id and total fails the row. It never reaches the unique index as a 23505. A hand-captured invoice with no external reference is adopted once when customer, total AND invoice date agree, and is stamped with the Sage id and number; a reference from another system conflicts. A staged row with no Sage id imports with no external reference, under `SAGE-<staging id>` when it has no number. A live invoice already carrying the Sage id also fails the row when it belongs to ANOTHER customer: that means the customer was renamed between runs, and booking it again would count the debt twice. The supplier side books a second bill in that case. A NEGATIVE staged total is a Sage credit note. It is marked `migration_status = 'credit_note'`, counted as skipped and reported as `customerInvoices.creditNotes` by `getMigrationStatus`, so a later credit-note import can find it. A zero total fails the row. Migration 694 adds `sage_customer_invoices.gl_customer_invoice_id`: the importer and `resetMigration('customer_invoices')` both named it, and both died on 42703. Both staging links (customer, and supplier from 205) are `ON DELETE SET NULL`, because `executeArchive` deletes old paid invoices and a NO ACTION link failed the archive run. A row with no invoice date fails. A staging row whose document was archived keeps 'imported' with a NULL link, and `resetMigration` re-pends it; so BOTH importers treat an invoice/bill held in `archive_customer_invoices` (by number: the archive keeps no external ref) or `archive_supplier_invoices` (by Sage id company-wide, so a supplier re-created under the same name still conflicts; or same supplier + number) as a conflict, or the re-run would book the settled debt again as live. `statedSageFigures` is gone, because no staging table states VAT any more.
- 2026-09-23 (R-119): **an invoice total may not be negative, and may not be NaN.** Migration 692 puts both rules on `customer_invoices` and `supplier_invoices` as a TRIGGER — not a CHECK, which is enforced even under `session_replication_role='replica'` and would make the rows already in production unseedable for the tests that must still handle them (R-117). NaN is the worse half: `NaN < 0` is FALSE so a sign test passes it, `NaN > 0` is TRUE so it passes the `balance > 0` filter the ageing and subledger use, and one such row makes `SUM()` NaN for the whole company. `assertNonNegativeDocumentTotal` (shared/documentTotalSign.ts) is the app-side twin — `Number.isFinite(t) && t >= 0`, never a bare sign test — wired into recurring-template execution (both sides), the AI capture pipeline, time-entry billing and both take-on importers, with `NegativeDocumentTotalError` mapped to 400 on the routes that can hit it. The Sage AR importer carries its own sign test, not this helper; since R-101 (2026-09-24) a negative staged total is set aside as a credit note. A legacy negative row can still be corrected, cancelled or converted; only writing a NEW negative is refused.
- 2026-09-23 (Hein's decision): **a supplier merge refuses when the two suppliers' `subject_to_drc_vat` flags differ** — `assertSupplierMergeKeepsDrcFlag` (duplicateMergeService), run by BOTH merge paths before anything moves (it is ALSO their existence/tenant check, and takes FOR UPDATE on both rows so a flag change cannot land between check and re-parenting): `mergeSuppliers` (duplicates-merge) and the inline-SQL `pages/api/accounting/supplier-merge.ts`. DRC VAT eligibility reads that flag, and a merge re-parents every bill. It throws `SupplierMergeRefusal`, which both routes return as a 400 with its message; both merge pages now show it (duplicates.tsx never checked `res.ok`; dedup.tsx read `body.message`, not `body.error.message`).

The REST create, the `PATCH /api/accounting/suppliers-list` flag-only route and MCP `create_supplier`/`update_supplier` (`subject_to_drc_vat`) all go through here. - 2026-09-23: `invoiceDateRangeParams.ts` — `parseInvoiceDateRange(query)` (Zod) and `isCalendarDate`, the one validator for the AR and AP invoice lists' inclusive `from_date`/`to_date`. Calendar-checked by string arithmetic; it never makes an instant out of a DATE.
- 2026-09-21: **The Sage supplier-invoice importer runs for the first time** (R-021, K-088, K-090). `sage_supplier_invoices` holds only `sage_id, invoice_number, supplier_name, invoice_date, total_amount`. The supplier is the ONE live supplier of that name on the company (case- and whitespace-insensitive); none or several fails the row. The due date is the invoice date plus `payment_terms` days, or NULL when the supplier has no terms. VAT is `deriveSageVat(null, null, total)`: none, and the bill carries the review note. A zero or negative total fails the row. The bill is imported unpaid and `approved`. Identity for a re-run after `resetMigration` is `(supplier, sage_invoice_id)`, then the unique key `(supplier, invoice_number)`, and the totals must agree; a live bill under that number with a different Sage id or total fails the row rather than absorbing it. A hand-captured bill with no Sage id and the same number and total is adopted once and stamped with the Sage id; it keeps its own dates and VAT split, not Sage's. The run holds `lockMigrationImport`. Every Sage run body goes through `withRunRecovery(runId, companyId, body)` (sageMigrationService), which rolls back to a savepoint before `failRun`, so the real error surfaces instead of 25P02; the 'failed' run row is inside the request transaction and does not survive the 500. `importCustomerInvoices` still SELECTs columns its table lacks (R-101; fixed 2026-09-24).

- 2026-09-10 (round 10): **extraction guesses, `unattendedPostingGate` decides.** Four rounds tried to
  PICK the payable out of several printed totals and each rule was beaten by a slip it had not seen

- 2026-09-09: `ocrAmountPatterns` — the guards and the patterns are now built from ONE LABEL
  VOCABULARY (`SEP`, `EXCL`, `INCL`, `VAT_WORD`, `TAX_WORD`, `NET_LABEL`, `NET_PREFIX`), because
  fixing one spelling at a time is how the same money defect came back three rounds running:

- 2026-09-09: `ocrAmountReconciliation` — where a PRINTED subtotal contradicts `total - VAT`
  (a levy or service charge printed below it), the derived net wins ONLY if the derived split
  looks standard-rated (13-17%); otherwise the printed figures stand and the caller refuses.
  Unconditional preference would silently rebase the split on a MIS-READ tax line. Either way the
  discrepancy is reported through `ExtractedAmounts.warnings`.
- 2026-09-09: `ocrAmountPatterns` — the label guards are VARIABLE-WIDTH, because the labels are.
  `(?<!Sub[-\s])` was fixed-width-one, so `Sub  Total` (any OCR column with more than one space)
  was still read as the payable total and the journal BALANCED at the VAT-exclusive figure.
  `NOT_A_SUBTOTAL` and the subtotal grammar now spell the same `Sub[\s-]*Total`. A new
  `NOT_A_TOTAL_LABEL` keeps "Total/Price Excluding VAT" out of the VAT candidates — without it a
  layout with no recognisable subtotal read VAT = 1000 and subtotal = 150 on an R1 150 invoice.
  The generic `Tax` form now ranks BELOW the bare `VAT` column so a tourism levy cannot outrank the
  tax, and `extractVatAmount` prefers the candidate the document's own arithmetic endorses
  (`subtotal + c === total`) over the first one printed. `AMOUNT` refuses to half-read a malformed
  figure: "1150.005" fails to match rather than coming back as 1150.00.
- 2026-09-09: **the recurring document is derived from its lines, auto-post actually posts, and the number retry is constraint-scoped (K-107 r4).** `recurringTemplateLines.ts` (new) DERIVES the header subtotal/tax/total from `templateData.lines` and refuses a stored aggregate that disagrees by more than 1c/line (capped at R1.00) with `RecurringTemplateTotalsMismatchError` — raised before the first write, so the route answers 400. Copying the aggregate across let a template whose lines came to R100 mint a header reading R9 999 / R11 499. Templates that predate the `lines` field still run on their aggregate. `auto_post` used to write `status = 'posted'`, which NEITHER status CHECK permits, so every auto-post template raised 23514 on every run for every tenant; both branches now call `approveCustomerInvoice` / `approveSupplierInvoice`, which is what writes the journal behind the document (a bare 'approved' would leave AR/AP without a GL). `insertWithReservedNumber` takes the numbering index name and renumbers ONLY for a clash on it — the attempt closure writes line items too, and any other 23505 used to burn four more numbers and surface the wrong cause. `reserveNextDocumentNumber` now bounds its wait on the counter row (`SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'`, restored on the SUCCESS path only) with `DocumentNumberLockTimeoutError`; it previously hung indefinitely behind a stuck holder.
- 2026-09-09: **the recurring runner's schedule is now its idempotency key (K-107).** `executeRecurring` read the template without `FOR UPDATE` and never consulted `next_run_date` — it only advanced it at the end. Nothing stopped a repeat run except an accident: the month-constant `RINV-<slug>-<YYYYMM>` number collided on `uq_customer_invoices_company_number`, so a second AR run in the same month died (and a genuine daily template died with it, while the AP side, having no unique index, silently minted an identical bill). Both branches now draw from the company sequence (`customer_invoice` / `supplier_invoice`, the same sequences every other writer uses) through `insertWithReservedNumber`, and migration 646 adds `uq_supplier_invoices_supplier_number`. That removed the accidental barrier, so `recurringTemplateLock.ts` puts a real one back: `FOR UPDATE` with a 5s `lock_timeout`, `is_due` computed in the same statement, and `RecurringTemplateNotDueError` raised BEFORE the first write so the route may answer 409. Both branches now also write line items from `templateData.lines`, inside the savepointed attempt. The `recurring_invoice` / RINV document type is retired: `getDocumentNumbers` filters it and the settings PUT refuses it up front (the row is hidden, not deleted — it holds the historical counter).
- 2026-09-09: **A document the migration wizard imports is a TAKE-ON, not an origination** (audit K-015 / R-001, R-002, R-020). `importARInvoices` and `importAPInvoices` post ONE two-line entry at `total_amount - amount_paid` — DR the control account, CR `opening_balance_equity` (mirrored for AP) — and **no revenue, expense or VAT line at all**. `buildTakeOnLines` in `migrationPostingSupport` is the single place that shape is decided; a document settled in full before the cutover creates the document and posts nothing, leaving `gl_journal_entry_id` NULL. The deciding reason is VAT: `getVATReturn` is GL-based and sweeps every posted `vat_input`/`vat_output` line with a NULL `vat_type` into boxes 1 and 15, so posting the invoice in full re-declared its VAT in a period that is usually already filed. Lines that are never written need no filter. Consequences worth knowing: (a) every take-on file now needs an `opening_balance_equity` account on the chart — `resolveTakeOnClearingAccountId` refuses the step up front, once, naming the role and the remedy; (b) `subtotal + tax` no longer has to equal `total` to the cent — up to 5c imports with a warning (persisted on the session as an `errors` entry with `severity: 'warning'`, so it survives a reload), beyond that the row is refused; (c) the trial balance may carry an AR or AP control total **instead of** the documents (a summary-only take-on) but never as well — `importOpeningBalances` records which control totals it accepted in `steps_completed` (`opening_balances_ar_control` / `_ap_control`) and `assertNoOpeningControlTotal` refuses the matching document step, and vice versa. The refusal in that direction is gated on `{ar,ap}_invoices_imported > 0` — documents actually TAKEN ON — not on the step flag, which is written even by a run that imported nothing and would otherwise bar the summary-only route for good; (d) `completeSession` records, but does not enforce, the `opening_balance_equity` residual for entries posted since the session started — it is a warning, and the message says the residual is expected when the whole trial balance was balanced on that account rather than accusing the operator of a double count. Both document steps AND `importOpeningBalances` take `lockMigrationImport` (a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed on the company) before reading the session: the interlock is a read-then-write both sides perform, and without it an overlapping pair each read a session without the other's mark and both post. `importOpeningBalances` (now in `migrationWizardOpeningBalanceService.ts`) is NOT a one-way door: it rewrites BOTH control flags from each run's own trial balance — including `false` — and reverses the entry its previous run posted for this session before posting the new one, so the remedy `assertNoOpeningControlTotal` prints ("remove the control account row and re-run the opening balances step") actually clears the refusal instead of posting a second full trial balance. Both invoice routes validate the body ROW BY ROW (`parseInvoiceRows` in `migrationRowSchemas`) rather than with one `safeParse`: a single bad line used to 400 all 5000 with a `fieldErrors` key of `invoices` and no row number. The rows that parse still import, and the services take an `ImportRowContext` so every `row` they report is a position in the operator's FILE, not in the shortened array. The persisted `severity: 'warning'` entries are read back by the migration hub (`SessionIssues` on `pages/accounting/migration/index.tsx`), which is what makes the durability real. WIZARD PATH ONLY: the Sage commit path posts its own journals and still re-declares VAT.
- 2026-09-09 (review round 3): **the counted refusal never reached the operator, and a scoped delete that matched nothing reported success.** Three layers each threw the message away. The page (`pages/accounting/cost-centres/index.tsx`) called `apiFetch` with no `res.ok` check inside an empty catch — `apiFetch` RESOLVES on 4xx, so the 400 was never an exception and Delete looked like a silent no-op. The route genericised every service error through `badRequestFromError(…, 'Action failed')` (pentest H16), so even a page that read the body got "Action failed"; the guard's refusal is written FOR the operator, so it now travels as **`CostCentreActionError`** and the route surfaces that type verbatim while everything else stays generic. And the whole page read `json.message`, but `apiResponse.error()` nests it at **`json.error.message`** — the convention `cashbook.tsx` and `my-account.tsx` already use. A browser run against a dev server is what caught the last two; the integration test asserting only `statusCode === 400` passed throughout. `deleteCostCentre` now carries `RETURNING id` and throws `Cost centre not found` when nothing matched, mirroring `toggleCostCentre` — a nonexistent id, an already-deleted id and another tenant's id used to return 200 `{ deleted: true }`. The guard also counts **`bank_transactions.cc1_id/cc2_id`** (no FK, written by `bankAllocationService` and the `save_selection` route; `bankAllocationService` copies the id onto the journal line at allocation, so a dangling value here becomes a dangling value in the ledger), and migration 660 makes `cost_centres.parent_id` RESTRICT — the children count is company-scoped and nothing constrains a parent and child to the same tenant, so a cross-tenant child was silently orphaned to NULL.
- 2026-09-09: **deleting a cost centre used to unassign every employee on it (K-110), and three counts were structurally always zero (K-111).** `deleteCostCentre` counted `gl_journal_lines` only, while `payroll_employees.cost_centre_id` (mig 450) was ON DELETE SET NULL and `assets.cost_centre_id` (mig 361) had no action clause — a payroll-only centre deleted cleanly and nulled every assignment, writing no `payroll_employee_history` row, so the assignment is unrecoverable. Eligibility now lives in **`costCentreUsageGuard.assertCostCentreUnused`**, which counts journal lines, journal entries, employees, employee allocations, assets, CHILD CENTRES (`cost_centres.parent_id` is SET NULL too, the same defect one column away), AP/AR documents and coding rules, and names each count in the refusal. Migration 649 makes the payroll and asset FKs RESTRICT, so the database refuses the delete even when the guard is bypassed; the guard is tenant-scoped and the FKs are not, so `deleteCostCentre` maps a cross-tenant 23503 back onto the same message rather than a 500. **Ten more cost-centre columns carry no FK at all** — the guard is the only thing standing between them and a dangling reference; add to the query, not to a new one, when a column joins them. `cost_centre_gl_mappings` (CASCADE, meaningless without its centre) and `capture_events.resolved_cost_centre_id` (an unposted classification hint) are deliberately outside it. Separately, `src/lib/neon.ts` resolves a tagged template to `res.rows`, so an UPDATE with no RETURNING resolves to `[]`: `duplicateMergeService` summed `rowCount` off a hand-written `SqlResult` cast (always undefined) and `timeTrackingService.submitEntries`/`approveEntries` read `length` off the same empty array, so a merge that moved three invoices reported 0. Every such statement now carries `RETURNING id` and counts `rows.length`; the cast type is gone so it cannot be re-made. The writes always landed — only the operator's feedback was wrong, and an operator reading "0 reassigned" as a failure who reverses the merge by hand moves live documents to the wrong supplier.
- 2026-09-09: `migrationOpeningBalanceService.postOpeningBalances` posts a balance on the side its SIGN implies, at its absolute value. It previously built `debit: isDebitNormal && openingBalance > 0 ? openingBalance : 0` and the credit mirror, so any account carrying a balance contrary to its normal side became a 0/0 line — and every outcome was a hard failure, so no wrong figure was ever stored: a source that actually foots was refused with totals that misstated the operator's own data, and when the discarded contras cancelled, `validateJournalEntry` rejected the zero-value lines. The `openingBalance !== 0` filter and the totals refusal are unchanged. **Known limit:** the entry is dated `new Date()` (the import date), not the take-on date, unlike the manual path which dates it at the open period's `start_date`; contra-carrying imports now reach this posting instead of always throwing, so they land in whatever period covers today.
- 2026-09-09: **`softDeleteJournalService` — soft-delete now moves the GENERAL LEDGER, not just `deleted_at`** (audit K-053). Approve posts a journal and cancel reverses it; soft-delete did neither, so once aging and the subledger started excluding a deleted document its debit stayed on the control account. `prepareInvoiceDelete` reverses the approval journal through the canonical `reverseJournalEntry` and `reinstateInvoiceJournal` puts it back on undo. Three things worth not re-deriving. (1) **The reversal id is RECORDED** (`soft_delete_journal_reversals`, migration 653) and the undo reverses THAT entry or nothing. Inferring it from the reversal chain — reverse a live head on delete, a dead one on undo — cannot tell a head this delete killed from one a user reversed on the GL screen, and `journal-entries-action.ts` leaves the invoice pointing at the reversed original where cancel NULLs the link; the undo then re-instated revenue and VAT output somebody had deliberately reversed, dated back into a closed period. (2) **`FOR UPDATE` on the journal row, not only the invoice row** — the racing GL-screen reversal never touches the invoice, so the invoice lock does not serialise it. (3) The delete refuses on `amount_paid` AND on live payment allocations, which is the full cancel guard: a draft payment allocated to a bill has not incremented `amount_paid` yet, and AP carries 397 production bills with `payment_matched = true` and `amount_paid = 0`. (4) **Refusal vs fault is decided by TYPE, and by no message text at all** (rounds 4-5). `SoftDeleteRefusalError` (`core/softDeleteErrors.ts`) is what the route answers 400 to; everything else is a fault and must stay a 500. The old `message.includes('not found')` test also matched `reverseJournalEntry`'s `Journal entry <id> not found` and `getSystemAccount`'s "... account not found", so a genuine data fault came back as a 400 carrying the raw internal message and never reached `log.error`. Round 4 still read one substring, `includes('fiscal period')`, for `resolveReversalDate`'s two plain Errors; those are `ReversalPeriodError` now (`gl/journalEntryPostingService`) and the arm is gone, because any unrelated fault mentioning a fiscal period was otherwise answered 400 with the internal message and never logged. `chainHead`'s unexpected-chain throw is a REFUSAL, not a fault: the walk follows posted rows only, so a reversal left un-posted empties the chain without any corruption, and a 500 there blocked the delete forever. (5) **Cancel refuses a soft-deleted document.** The delete keeps `gl_journal_entry_id` pointing at the (now reversed) original so the undo can find it; cancel locked the row with no `deleted_at` filter and would flip the status and NULL the link, after which an undo re-instates the journal of a document the sub-ledger excludes as cancelled. Both `customerInvoiceCancelService` and `supplierInvoiceWorkflowService` now carry `AND deleted_at IS NULL` on the `FOR UPDATE` read. (6) **`purgeExpiredDeletes` is coupled to all of this and has no caller.** Hard-DELETEing a soft-deleted invoice destroys the only row the dated presence predicate can evaluate, so every as-at date before the delete loses the document from the sub-ledger side while the GL still carries it, permanently. It also stranded the `soft_delete_journal_reversals` row, which has no FK to the invoice; the purge now deletes it in the same pass, scoped by (company_id, entity_id) pairs.
- 2026-09-02: `migrationCoaService.importChartOfAccounts` validates before writing: `validateSystemAccountMap` refuses the WHOLE import on an unknown role key, a code not in the payload, or an account whose type cannot carry the role (an expense as `vat_input`) — the map's keys become `account_subtype` + `is_system_account = true` verbatim and the resolver hands those rows to every auto-posting path. Each non-mapped row's own `accountSubtype` goes through `subtypeErrorFor` like every other write path. `clearSystemAccountCache(companyId)`, not the whole cache.
- 2026-08-31: **the categorisation defaults no longer invent a VAT claim.** `learnFromAllocation` wrote `vat_code = vatCode || 'standard'`, so learning a restaurant into Staff Welfare minted a pattern claiming input tax on entertainment, which the rule auto-post path then honoured on every future charge; `findPatternMatch` had the same `p.vat_code || 'standard'` fallback. Both now default to 'none' — a missing code is not evidence of a claimable supply — and `learnFromAllocation` runs the account's own denial (`resolveVatCodeForAccount`) over an explicit 'standard'. Migration 521 rewrites the patterns already learned against denied accounts.
- 2026-08-15: `companyAccessService` added (`userBelongsToCompany` / `userBelongsToGroup`), replacing four duplicated inline guards in `company-groups.ts`, `consolidated-reports.ts`, `intercompany-transactions.ts` and `permissions.ts`. **16** `text = uuid` sites fixed — 13 `company_users.user_id = ${x}::UUID`, 2 `users.id = ${x}::UUID`, and 1 uncast `users.id` join. Each threw a 500 on every call, killing group access (so the consolidation dashboard was unreachable even after its queries were repaired in #249), company user management, the pentest-H4 permission guard, POPIA export **and erasure**, and credit-note PDFs. `approvalService` and `practiceReportsService` already carried the correct `::TEXT` and were NOT broken — an earlier draft of this note claimed 18 sites and named them; blind review caught it. New CI step `user-id-casts` blocks the class, with its rules unit-tested in `tests/unit/ci/userIdCastRules.test.ts`.
